claims.statement: Joint CircuitBreaker theorem under rules.md: the following declaration defines ONE fixed eligible total uniform NP family in the pinned full B2 model at actual input length n. Its full guarantee and its declared projection both hold unconditionally, for all sufficiently large integer lengths with the quantifiers specified by the theorem kinds. Both score source claims assert this ENTIRE declaration, not separate lemmas. For g(n)=c*n^p*(log2 n)^q*(log2 log2 n)^r with the exact parameters in guarantee, liminf over all integer n of C_B2(f_n)/g(n) >= 1. Equivalently, for every epsilon>0 there is N_epsilon such that C_B2(f_n)>=(1-epsilon)*g(n) for every integer n>=N_epsilon. Declaration: {"convention":"uniform-np-full-b2-actual-length-all-lengths-v1","family":"The OR family: f_0(empty input)=0; for every n>=1, f_n(x_1,...,x_n)=x_1 OR ... OR x_n, the characteristic function of the total language L={x in {0,1}* : x contains a 1}. One fixed total family defined at every length, with the uniform linear-time evaluator and empty-witness NP verifier given in proof.md.","guarantee":{"coefficient":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"1"},"exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"1"},"kind":"polynomial_log","log_exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"0"},"loglog_exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"0"}},"projection":{"coefficient":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"1"},"exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"1"},"kind":"finite"},"theorem":"For this one fixed total uniform polynomial-time family, hence in NP with empty witnesses, C_B2(f_n)=n-1 for all n>=1 (and C_B2(f_0)=0), so liminf as n tends to infinity of C_B2(f_n)/n >= 1 in the full Li-Yang B2 model at actual input length n=|x|. Equivalently, for every epsilon>0 there is N_epsilon such that C_B2(f_n)>=(1-epsilon)*n for every integer n>=N_epsilon.","version":"circuitbreaker-expression-v1"}

claims: Unscored lemma (tightness): for the OR family of bound.json, C_B2(f_n) = n-1 for every n >= 1 and C_B2(f_0) = 0 in the pinned full B2 model; proved in proof.md (Sections 4-5) via the essential-input connectivity lower bound and the binary OR-tree upper bound. Hence no coefficient above 1 at exponent 1 holds for this family.
title: Coefficient/exponent pair (1, 1) for the fixed OR family in NP (self-contained proof)
